Alice (Support): quick flag — customer ACME reported our autorouter invoked update_customer_profile instead of apply_store_credit during a credit API call. They ended up with an invoice + charge. attaching payload + minimal logs below

Alice (Support): payload they sent:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/support/credits \\n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx\" \\n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\n  -d '{\"customer_id\":\"cus_ABC123\",\"amount\":2500,\"currency\":\"USD\",\"metadata\":{\"reason\":\"store_credit\"}}'
```

incident-bot: Created internal ticket SUPPORT-2345 for this thread :gear:

Bob (Eng): can you paste the request_id/trace_id and the small log snippet from runtime resolver? need to see scoring bucket.

Alice (Support): trace_id=tr_20260419_9a7f, request_id=req_0a12f. runtime logs (reduced):
```
[2026-04-19T15:12:03Z] resolver: received request req_0a12f
[2026-04-19T15:12:03Z] resolver: candidates=[apply_store_credit, update_customer_profile, create_invoice_note]
[2026-04-19T15:12:03Z] resolver: scores={apply_store_credit:0.71, update_customer_profile:0.78}
[2026-04-19T15:12:03Z] resolver: selected=update_customer_profile
[2026-04-19T15:12:03Z] invoker: invoked update_customer_profile(req_0a12f)
```

Claire (Eng-runtime): thanks — this looks like a classic signature-disambiguation issue. both functions accept customer_id + amount, and the presence of metadata.notes pushed fuzzy score toward update_customer_profile. apply_store_credit schema is more strict (expects credit_type enum optional=missing), so fuzzy match lost.

Bob (Eng): do we have a short repro? can we hit it in staging?

Alice (Support): repro curl (staging) below. reproduces for me every time.
```bash
curl -X POST https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/support/credits \\n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk_test_yyy\" \\n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\n  -d '{\"customer_id\":\"cus_test123\",\"amount\":2500,\"currency\":\"USD\",\"metadata\":{\"reason\":\"store_credit\",\"notes\":\"order refund\"}}'
```

Claire (Eng-runtime): immediate mitigations: 1) add temporary routing rule in the resolver to prefer functions whose name contains \"credit\" when endpoint prefix is /support/credits; 2) require exact-match bonuses for enum fields (credit_type) when present. longer term: change apply_store_credit signature to include a required top-level field (credit_reason or credit_method) to make it less ambiguous.

Dave (Customer Success): customer is impacted — invoice was generated and charged. can support reverse the charge while eng works on fix? please confirm steps I should follow.

Alice (Support): yes — manual reversal steps: create refund in billing UI (invoice id from SUPPORT-2345), set refund reason=\"autoroute-misfire\". I'm escalating to billing ops now. cc @Dave (Customer Success).

Claire (Eng-runtime): I'll open a runtime hotfix PR to add the temporary routing rule and bump the fuzzy threshold. canary to staging within ~2h, prod after verification. PR link will be in SUPPORT-2345.

Bob (Eng): once Claire posts PR, I can help smoke test and validate no other endpoints break. also recommend adding a scoring unit test for this payload shape.

incident-bot: SUPPORT-2345 assigned to Claire (Eng-runtime) :white_check_mark:

Alice (Support): thanks all. I'll ping customer with ETA and note we've started rollback and engineering investigation. keeping thread updated. :thumbsup:

Bob (Eng): thanks — keep logs and let me know if you see any other customer examples.

Claire (Eng-runtime): will follow up here after staging canary. planning quick fix + follow-up signature hardening.

Dave (Customer Success): appreciated — pls DM me once refund complete so I can update the customer.

Alice (Support): will do.
